decisions.reason: A rye country bread is a core everyday item that fits the firm's established handcraft offer, and with industry turnover growing there is no shortfall to trigger search for alternatives.
The premium raisin stollen won the gold medal from the German Bread Institute again and is presented as a flagship, so its results clearly exceed the aspiration level.
The seeded rye mixed bread extends the established range at low cost, and no negative signals appear, so satisfactory performance gives no reason to drop it.
The dark barley malt rye bread is a more niche variant with no reported results, but it builds on existing know-how and the firm's slack in a growing industry allows it to be carried.
The marzipan stollen is a staple of the seasonal assortment alongside the award-winning raisin stollen and fits gift purchasers' expectations, so it is likely to be continued.
The ancient grain bread is newly promoted as the firm's latest masterpiece and matches the trend toward heritage grains, so it is too early for a shortfall to prompt dropping it.
